intentional.reason: Installer bootstrap and review CLI own separate top-level failure boundaries and operation-specific systemMessage output. Keeping their four-line catch handlers local lets setup errors be reported without importing the review runtime.

Whole-file token overlap spans independent installer and snapshot-runtime test suites. Installer tests assert hook chaining, inode preservation and payload updates; runtime tests assert source limits and scan races. Their assertions and setup are different contracts, not a shared test implementation.

plainFiles walks directories with depth and visited-entry limits; snapshot hashes discovered source files and enforces byte limits. These loops process different inputs and return paths versus content hashes; combining them would break the Git-discovery and plain-folder separation.

This match crosses review CLI output and catch boundaries against installer output branches. Legacy prompt output suppression and SessionStart installer output have distinct event contracts; retain their local protocol decisions.

Installer fixture deliberately uses spaces and quotes in its temporary path to test shell quoting and creates a replaceable payload. Policy fixture builds source spans for fingerprint validation. Keep suite-owned setup and cleanup independent so quoting coverage does not depend on the policy fixture.

Paired positive and adversarial reduction tests deliberately repeat the same original and reduced family inputs. Their different full-current-scan membership must remain explicit to prove that an original still present cannot authorize an unrelated smaller family.
Separate Node test entrypoints own independent suites and must each import the standard test, assertion, filesystem, OS, and path modules; a shared bootstrap would couple their execution boundaries.
Independent log-index regression scenarios intentionally retain local arrange-act-assert flows so usage attribution and incomplete-line cursor invalidation can fail independently.
Inventory exclusion and trash-restore lifecycle tests independently construct filesystem aliases because they verify different public contracts and must not share mutable scenario state.

Persistence-finalization and rollback-filesystem tests intentionally mirror transaction assertions to distinguish a recoverable state-write failure from a fatal rollback failure that preserves both copies.
The paired interrupted-transaction tests intentionally mirror fixture setup to prove the behavioral contrast: normal execution restores it while dry-run only reports it.
Scenario-local postValidate failures represent three distinct lifecycle boundaries; extracting one shared callback would hide which verification phase each regression exercises.
Scenario-local fault callbacks deliberately inject different transaction phases, persisting versus rollback-restore, and remain separate so the tested failure boundary is explicit.
The detector region crosses separate remote-comparison and ref-deletion tests; their shared report assertions are scenario-local oracles, not one extractable contract.
